issues.summary: Rename test_GET_sorts_by_name to reflect id-based ordering
issues.detail: The test at src/maasserver/api/tests/test_networks.py:90 now asserts ordering by subnet.id, matching the handler's order_by("id") in NetworksListingForm.filter_subnets; it never exercised name sorting. The misleading name invites a future regression back to lexicographic comparison; rename to test_GET_sorts_by_id (line 93/90, outside the hunk).

issues.summary: Drop the redundant sorted() over already id-ascending factory subnets
issues.detail: At src/maasserver/api/tests/test_networks.py:104, subnets is built by sequential factory.make_Subnet() calls, so it is already in ascending-id order; sorted(subnets, key=lambda subnet: subnet.id) is a no-op. Keeping it is defensible as an explicit ordering guard, but the actual fix is comparing ids rather than lexicographically sorting "subnet-<id>" strings.

issues.summary: Remove the unused name= kwarg from the subnet fixtures
issues.detail: Line 93 passes name=factory.make_name("subnet").lower() to factory.make_Subnet(), but neither the handler nor the new assertion uses the subnet name field; convert_to_network_name returns "subnet-%d" % subnet.id (src/maasserver/api/networks.py:23-25). The fixture argument is actively misleading alongside the sorts_by_name test name.
